accuracy.evidence: Checked against Development Matters (2021) mathematics for 3 and 4 year olds (talk about and identify patterns; extend and create ABAB patterns, stick, leaf, stick, leaf; notice and correct an error in a repeating pattern), the Reception statement (continue, copy and create repeating patterns) and the Head Start ELOF patterning goal (recognise, duplicate and extend simple patterns). Every lab string was rechecked by hand: rbrbr continues b r b, gygyg continues y g y, ccsccs continues c c s, and the three fix rows each have exactly one break (positions 4, 6 and 5). The all-one-colour caveat in the adult text is stated precisely rather than calling it not a pattern.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips documented for this age in pattern research (Rittle-Johnson et al. 2015; Lüken 2012): repeating the last item instead of alternating (prediction Red or Blue after red, challenge tag same), bringing in a new item (tag new), AAB collapsed to AB (clap, clap, stamp prediction and car, car, bus tag swap), treating a jumbled row or a single unit as a pattern (tags random and short), and not checking from the start when fixing (tags first and fine).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagabab is a bead-string machine for repeating patterns at 3 to 4: the next-gap continue rule, bead-by-bead copying against a model row, a clap and stamp rhythm row, a single-break fixer, and a unit-of-repeat builder that the machine repeats three times. flagpat (Spotting Patterns, 7 to 8) is about number rules and testing a rule on every step; flagsort sorts by attribute. The shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the rule by filling gaps that only accept the bead the unit predicts, and each wrong drop names the unit aloud (Say the colours: red, blue, red, blue). Copying shows order matters; the clap row moves the same idea to sounds; the fixer makes them say the row from the start; and the builder makes the unit explicit by highlighting the start of each repeat with a ring. Each idea is done first and only named in the done message.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: Red after red, blue, red, blue, red (the gap refuses red), Stamp after clap, clap, stamp, clap, clap, stamp (the row only accepts clap), and Yes for red, blue, red, red, red, blue (the fixer shows bead 4 breaks it). A.reveal quotes the child's guess in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers and a specific correction for each: same (it swaps every time), new (nothing new comes in), swap (one more car before the bus), random (does not repeat the same part), short (once is not enough to see it repeat), first (the first one starts the pattern) and fine (the 4th should be blue). Lab drops also name the slip, for example Look at the top row. Bead 3 is blue.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short read-aloud sentences (Look: red, blue, red, blue. It goes again and again.) and pass the family kid limit in validate_lessons; the adult text stays under the family adult limit while using the precise early maths terms repeating pattern, ABAB and AAB, unit of repeat (core), copy, continue or extend, create, and correct an error.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and explanation overlap with every lesson, including Spotting Patterns and Sorting by colour, size and shape, is under the 12 percent limit. Each kid paragraph adds one move (see it, say it, sounds too, fix it and make one); the adult paragraphs give the curriculum statements, the unit of repeat idea, four named mistakes with a caution, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on a 360 px Android and iPhone 13 in dark and light: the tray beads are about 90 px across with a shape mark (circle, square, triangle, diamond), the row of eight slots fits with the next gap ringed in violet, the fixer's six beads are about 50 px with numbered 1 to 6 buttons below, and the builder's three big slots and Repeat it! button are reachable. Nothing is clipped in either theme.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, every Show me completed (5 tasks) and the challenge showed. Every drag has a button twin (Red, Blue, Yellow, Green, Clap, Stamp, bead 1 to 6 labelled with its colour, Repeat it!, Clear), colour is never the only cue because each bead carries a shape, and the canvas aria-label speaks each change, for example Blue. 2 more to go.
